question: What defines a very ill patient in a clinical setting?

options.A: Mild chronic illness requiring routine checkups
options.B: Walk-in patients seeking outpatient malaria treatment
options.C: Acute physiological instability and organ dysfunction
options.D: Stable postoperative recovery on a general ward

explanation: Very ill patients suffer from critical disruptions in their vital life systems that demand continuous observation. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h1)

question: The primary clinical objective when nursing a very ill patient is what?

options.A: Discharging the patient within twenty four hours
options.B: Preventing further deterioration and stabilizing vitals
options.C: Reducing the cost of hospital medications
options.D: Gathering detailed family medical history records

explanation: Critical care nursing centers on stopping decline and supporting failing body systems. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which tool assesses the level of consciousness in a critical patient?
explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale measures eye, verbal, and motor responses to evaluate brain function. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why is regular trend analysis of vital signs vital for very ill patients?

options.A: It eliminates the need for laboratory investigations
options.B: It catches subtle physiological declines before crisis hits
options.C: It fulfills mandatory hospital record-keeping bureaucracy
options.D: It proves the nurse is working night shifts

explanation: Watching patterns over time reveals hidden deterioration faster than a single isolated reading. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the absolute first priority when managing a very ill patient?

options.B: Ensuring a clear and patent airway

explanation: Without oxygen delivery to the lungs and brain, all other resuscitation efforts fail. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h3)

question: An unconscious patient is positioned on their side primarily to achieve what purpose?

options.A: Preventing aspiration of oral secretions and vomitus
options.B: Making it easier to change bed linens
options.C: Reducing pressure ulcers on the sacrum
options.D: Improving blood flow to the lower extremities

explanation: Lateral positioning allows fluids to drain out of the mouth rather than pooling in the trachea. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h3)

question: How is fluid balance tracked accurately in a critically ill patient?

options.B: Weighing the patient once every week
options.C: Asking the family how much water was drunk

explanation: Recording every milliliter of fluid entering and leaving the body reveals renal and circulatory status. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is enteral tube feeding often necessary for very ill patients?

options.B: It completely stops the digestive tract from working
options.C: They are too weak or unconscious to swallow safely
options.D: It is cheaper than buying hospital drugs

explanation: Compromised consciousness or extreme weakness prevents normal oral intake, risking aspiration. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h4)

question: How often should an immobile, very ill patient be turned in bed?
explanation: Turning every two hours relieves constant pressure on bony prominences, preventing skin breakdown. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h5)

question: Hypostatic pneumonia in bedridden patients is best prevented by doing what?

options.A: Applying medicated creams to the chest wall
options.B: Restricting all oral fluids to dry the lungs
options.C: Frequent repositioning and deep breathing encouragement
options.D: Keeping the room completely dark and warm

explanation: Movement and deep breaths mobilize pooled respiratory secretions, preventing bacterial growth in the lungs. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h5)

question: How can a nurse assess pain in a patient who cannot speak?

options.A: Checking the patient's temperature with a thermometer
options.B: Waiting until the patient recovers consciousness to ask
options.C: Assuming pain is absent if the patient is sleeping
options.D: Observing facial grimacing, restlessness, and vital sign changes

explanation: Non-verbal cues like frowning, tachycardia, and tense muscles indicate distress when speech is impossible. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which intervention directly promotes physical comfort for a bedridden patient?

options.A: Adjusting bed positioning and smoothing wrinkled sheets
options.B: Withdrawing pain medication to prevent addiction
options.D: Turning off all lights for forty eight hours

explanation: Removing physical irritants like crumbs or wrinkles reduces skin friction and muscle tension. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why should nurses continue talking to an unconscious, very ill patient?

options.B: It replaces the need for pain medication
options.C: Hearing is often the last sense to fade
options.D: It proves the patient is fully awake

explanation: Auditory perception often remains active even when a patient appears completely unresponsive. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h7)

question: A distressed family member of a critical patient needs what primary support from the nurse?

options.A: Strict orders to stop asking questions
options.B: Medical textbooks to read about the disease
options.D: Complete restriction from visiting the ward

explanation: Clear communication reduces anxiety and helps families cope with the uncertainty of critical illness. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary shift in goals when a patient enters end-of-life care?

options.A: Focusing on comfort, dignity, and pain relief
options.B: Discharging the patient immediately to save beds
options.C: Aggressive pursuit of curative experimental surgeries
options.D: Stopping all forms of nursing documentation

explanation: Palliative care prioritizes quality of life and peaceful symptom management over curative efforts. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing responsibility during terminal care?

options.A: Providing emotional support to grieving relatives
options.C: Managing distressing symptoms like pain and dyspnea

explanation: Curative therapies are stopped at the end of life because the focus shifts entirely to comfort. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h8)
